name: Ingersoll Rand Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate-to-strong installed-base moat: ~37% of sales are recurring aftermarket parts/service on mission-critical compressors and vacuum equipment, #2 global position behind Atlas Copco with multi-brand coverage and a proven bolt-on M&A machine, plus a net-cash balance sheet. Capped at 6 because Atlas Copco is the stronger premium benchmark, China pricing is actively compressing margins (-160bp adj. EBITDA margin in Q2 2026), equipment demand is cyclical, and growth is substantially acquired rather than organic — FY2025 already took a $273.4M goodwill/intangible impairment.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Quality aftermarket-driven compounder with a real installed-base moat, but owner's earnings are flat for 3 years and at $78.43 the weighted IRR is only 8.22% — even the super bull (13.37%) misses the 15% hurdle; clears 15% only at the weighted IV of $33.75.
moat_for: Installed base drives ~37% of sales as recurring aftermarket parts and service
#2 global position in industrial air behind Atlas Copco, multi-brand coverage
Mission-critical products with high customer downtime costs — service/parts stickiness
Proven bolt-on M&A machine plugging niche leaders into the global service network
Net cash balance sheet (-$1,247.4M net debt) funds M&A and buybacks
moat_against: Atlas Copco is the premium benchmark with deeper service coverage and tech
China pricing pressure compressing margins (adj. EBITDA margin -160bp YoY Q2 2026)
Cyclical industrial capex demand; organic growth was negative in recent quarters
Growth substantially bought via M&A — integration/goodwill risk ($273.4M impairment in FY2025)
No network effects or contractual lock-in; customers run mixed, dual-sourced fleets
